q: How do I count emissions from a charcoal tandoor in a restaurant?
title: Charcoal tandoor emissions
short: CO2 from burning charcoal made from wood is biogenic, so report it separately from Scope 1. The methane and nitrous oxide from burning still count in Scope 1, and charcoal making releases methane upstream (Scope 3). An LPG or electric tandoor moves emissions to fossil Scope 1 or to Scope 2.

ul: Kg of charcoal bought each month, from invoices.
Supplier and whether it is wood or coal-based.
LPG tandoor: 2.98 kg CO2 per kg of LPG, fossil Scope 1.

sections.h: If the charcoal is from coal
p: Coal-based briquettes are fossil, so their CO2 counts fully in Scope 1.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
